core_obligations: Invoke the pseudo-coherent statement to get that K is pseudo-coherent and that K tensor^L_A A_n -> K_n is an isomorphism for all n (proof lines 28422-28424).

For a surjection A -> kappa with kernel a maximal ideal m, use that any element of A mapping to a unit in A_1 is a unit in A to conclude that Ker(A -> A_1) is contained in the Jacobson radical of A, and hence that A -> kappa factors through A -> A_1 (proof lines 28425-28431).
Use that factorisation to obtain the chain K tensor^L_A kappa = K tensor^L_A A_1 tensor^L_{A_1} kappa = K_1 tensor^L_{A_1} kappa (proof lines 28432-28437).

Since K_1 is perfect by assumption (2), use that a perfect complex has finite tor dimension to find integers a and b with H^i(K tensor^L_A kappa) = 0 for all i outside [a, b] (proof lines 28438-28441).
Apply the pointwise perfection criterion to conclude that K is perfect (proof lines 28442-28443).
difficulty_reason: The lemma takes A = lim A_n a limit of an inverse system of rings, objects K_n of D(A_n) with compatible maps K_{n+1} -> K_n, and assumes that the transition maps A_{n+1} -> A_n are surjective with locally nilpotent kernels; that either all K_n are perfect or there is n_0 beyond which K_{n_0} is perfect and the kernels are nilpotent; and that the maps induce isomorphisms K_{n+1} tensor^L_{A_{n+1}} A_n -> K_n; it concludes that K = R lim K_n is perfect in D(A) with K tensor^L_A A_n -> K_n an isomorphism for all n (source lines 28400-28419). The proof begins from the pseudo-coherent statement, which already gives that K is pseudo-coherent and that the base change maps are isomorphisms (proof lines 28422-28424). The substantive part is the reduction to a residue field computation. For a surjection A -> kappa with kernel a maximal ideal m, the proof uses that any element mapping to a unit in A_1 is a unit in A to conclude that Ker(A -> A_1) lies in the Jacobson radical of A, so that A -> kappa factors through A -> A_1 (proof lines 28425-28431). Hence the displayed chain gives K tensor^L_A kappa = K tensor^L_A A_1 tensor^L_{A_1} kappa = K_1 tensor^L_{A_1} kappa (proof lines 28432-28437). Since K_1 is perfect by assumption (2), it has finite tor dimension, so there are integers a and b with H^i(K tensor^L_A kappa) = 0 for all i outside [a, b] (proof lines 28438-28441); the pointwise perfection criterion then gives that K is perfect (proof lines 28442-28443). The non-routine content is the radical argument that descends the residue field through A_1 and the use of the pointwise criterion.
